summary: Federated identity exchange failing for Dedicated LLM provisioning due to conditional binding mismatch
description: Issue summary: During provisioning of a Dedicated capacity cluster for an enterprise customer in APAC, the federated identity exchange between GCP Workload Identity and the AWS assume-role path fails. Impact: new Dedicated clusters cannot complete bootstrap, delaying customer onboarding and blocking reserve capacity assignment. Observed failures are intermittent (approx 60% of attempts) and correlate with requests routed through our org-level identity broker. Affects onboarding pipeline and automated e2e validation jobs.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger dedicated-provisioner for customer account (apac project) using onboarding pipeline.
2) Provisioner requests a GCP WorkloadIdentity -> exchange token with internal federation broker.
3) Broker attempts AWS AssumeRole with externalId and session tags.
4) AWS returns AccessDenied with message referencing Tag/Session policy or missing PrincipalTag.
5) Provisioner retries; sometimes succeeds on 2nd attempt.
Observed via CI runs and manual repro from staging account.
logs: GCP STS response: 'aud mismatch' seen in some traces; AWS STS error: 'AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/dedicated-provisioner-role because PrincipalTag condition failed'. Correlation id: c7f8b2d4. Timestamps: 2026-03-09T19:12:21Z, 2026-03-10T03:07:44Z. Detailed curl of broker exchange and full stack traces attached to ticket (sanitized).
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Org-level tag-enforcing policy on AWS may strip or alter session tags during cross-account assume; 2) WorkloadIdentity audience formatting mismatch intermittently causes AWS to reject token; 3) Broker is not consistently mapping GCP service account attributes to expected AWS session tags/ExternalId. Observed that successful and failed traces differ in the 'x-goog-iam-authorization' header and session tag set. Sample trace comparison saved in linked Confluence page.
actions_taken:
- Scoped logs collected from broker, provisioner, and STS calls.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive retry backoff to surface first-failure details.
- Ran targeted repro in a controlled apac project with debug-level tracer enabled; reproduced 3/5 attempts failing.
- Escalated to cloud-identity infra team: asked for policy eval on AWS accounts and org SCPs.
- Added extra validation to provisioner to log session tag payload and ExternalId before STS call.
next_steps:
- Coordinate with Cloud Security to run policy simulator on the target AWS account to identify which condition blocks the assume-role (due by 2026-03-14).
- Short-term mitigation: relax tag-based condition in the dedicated-provisioner role to accept missing optional tags while we remediate mapping. Deploy change to staging, run 20 repros.
- Long-term: standardize session tag mapping in federation broker and add a signature of mapping version to logs; update onboarding runbook.
- Owner: Diego Alvarez; ETA for mitigation deploy: 2026-03-14.
resolution: (Pending) Root cause under active investigation. Temporary mitigation planned to relax restrictive tag condition on the AWS assume-role for onboarding accounts. Full resolution will include changes to federation broker mapping and an org-policy gap remediation. Once the mitigation is validated in staging and apac repros pass 20/20, we'll roll to prod and update onboarding docs and runbook.
